answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents submit cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs, anchoring identity without leaking secrets. The protocol imposes exponential capital exhaustion where staking collateral scales superlinearly with swarm size: the n-th clone costs O(k^n). A rogue entity cannot harbor fake identities when each unverified node is marked as a sable risk, turning any stolen relic of past credentials useless against the escalating cost.
